title: CLCON/190/2012 of TABASSUM KHAN Vs J.P. SHARMA

paras.text:
CLCON 338 of 2011
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Shri A.S. Rawat, Senior Advocate assisted
by Shri Raveendra Singh Bisht, Advocate for the
petitioner.
 Shri Sunil Upadhyaya, Advocate for the
State/respondents.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that the petitioner is not pressing the
petition against the respondent no. 1, who has
wrongly been impleaded in the contempt
petition. The contempt petition against
respondent no. 1 is dismissed.
List again.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
mamta 19.11.2012

WPSS No. 1199 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Ms. Anjali Noliyal, Advocate for the
petitioner.
 Shri Ashish Joshi, learned Standing
Counsel for the State/respondents.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that petitioner has completed his
one-year computer course from Shikhar Aptech
Computer Education which is recognized by the
H.N.B (P.G.) Colleage, Khatima. She further
submitted that the respondent have given
appointment two candidates who have
completed their computer course from the same
institute.
 Learned Standing counsel prays for and is
granted time till next Monday i.e. 26.11.2012
for filing counter affidavit.
 List thereafter.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
mamta 19.11.2012

WPSS No. 583 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Shri Alok Mahra, Advocate for the
petitioners.
 Shri Ashish Joshi, learned Standing
Counsel for the State/respondents.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 On 31st October, 2012 this Court is
directed to standing counsel to file the
supplementary counter affidavit stating therein
the basis for differentiating the institutions. The
State Government is also directed to furnish list
of those institutions, which have been
recognized by the State Government or by the
competent authority. The respondent no. 2 file
supplementary counter affidavit. Same be taken
on record. In Para 4 of the supplementary
counter affidavit the respondent no. 2 gave the
institutions name and computer certificate
issued by the DOEACC Department of
Electronics Accredited Computer Course,
HILTRON, Garhwal and Kumaon Universities are
recognized. The supplementary counter affidavit
filed by the respondent no. 2 is confusing.
Learned Standing counsel prays for and is
allowed further one week time to file another
supplementary counter affidavit.
List this case on 26.11.2012.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
mamta 19.11.2012

WPSS No. 633 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Shri Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the
petitioner.
 Shri Ashish Joshi, learned Standing
Counsel for the State/respondents.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that petitioner passed her
certificate course, which is annexed
annexure 36 of the petition. The petitioner
completed her one-year diploma Course in
Office Automation & Publishing from Rajeev
Gandhi Computer Saksharta Mission, Koshi
Kalan, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh. He
submitted that the above course is
recognized/approved by the Singhania
University, Jhunjhunu, Rajashthan and thus
the petitioner is eligible to participate the
process of selection.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner also
referred the letter written by the
automation body affiliated by the other
State Government and also by which other
State in which the employment exchanges
.........to enrolled such candidate who has
completed above course from the Rajeev
Gandhi Computer Saksharta Mission, Koshi
Kalan, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.
List this matter on next Monday i.e.
26.11.2012, by that time Sate
Government/respondents are directed to
verify this fact, whether the course duly
recognized any of the State Government.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) mamta 19.11.2012

CLCON 338 of 2011
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

CLCON 147 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Shri Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate for
the petitioners.
 Shri Rajesh Sharma, learned Brief
Holder for the State/respondents.
 List this matter on 03.12.2012 in daily
cause list.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
mamta 19.11.2012

CLCON No. 190 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Ms. Tabassum Khan, applicant is
present in person.
Shri Mahendra Pratap, present for the
respondent.
 Ms. Tabassum Khan, applicant
appeared in the Court. She submitted that
since the order has not passed by the
respondent rejecting the representation of
the petitioner. She does not wish to pursue
the contempt petition and she will file fresh
petition for challenging in this regard.
 In view of the statement of Ms.
Tabassum Khan, the contempt petition is
dismissed as not press.
(V.K. Bist, J.)
mamta 19.11.2012
